Rammeaftalen omfatter levering af den udbudte ydelse til Ordregivers lokationer i hele Danmark, inkl. ikke-brofaste øer. Der forventes dog alene et mindre behov for levering af ydelser til ikke-brofaste øer. Rammeaftalen indgås med to leverandører. Opgaver, der tildeles på grundlag af Rammeaftalen, tildeles direkte på de vilkår, der er fastsat i Rammeaftalen, herunder de aftalte priser og øvrige kontraktvilkår. Som udgangspunkt tildeles alle opgaver til 1. prioritetsleverandøren. 2. prioritetsleverandøren tildeles alene en opgave i de i Rammeaftalens pkt. 8 angivne situationer.

title: AEROTHERMODYNAMIC CHARACTERIZATION OF GAS-SURFACE INTERACTIONS FOR HYPERSONIC UPPER STAGE RECOVERY VEHICLES - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To model the hypersonic flow around critical points of the re-entry of a upper stage vehicle, accounting for the catalytic properties of a Si-O-C ceramics, and for the chemical modifications of the surface exposed to the air.Description: There is a renewed interest in the implementation of reusable vehicles for in-orbit operation. A critical aspect in the lifetime of a space vehicle is to improve the durability of the thermal protection structures, to limit the replacement of the thermal shield. Ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTC) materials, based on the Si-O-C compounds with dedicated coatings (boride, molybdenum etc.) demonstrated to be a good choice, due to their capability to resist and survive above 1500 K. To fully evaluate the response of any material in suchextreme operating conditions, it is also imperative to determine the catalysis in high temperature gas, strongly affecting the surface heat flux. Moreover, the interaction of the material coatings with dissociated gases such as oxygen and nitrogen, induces variations on the material properties. The model will include advanced kinetics, using a hybrid state-to-state -Multi-Temperature (StS-MT) derived from the StS, where the vibrational degrees of freedom are described by the vibrational temperature, while electronic excited states are treated as independent species, in order to estimate the radiative properties.
